Google Drive - current commercial release record and April 2026 lane doctrine; identifiers withheld from this public repository

open_questions: Two private repositories in the account are named or described as a command center and could not be attached. What is in them, and does this control plane duplicate them?
Should the control plane live in a public repository at all, or move to a private one?
Which February 2026 governance-architecture document controls, if any?
Does the Cross-Lane tag in the April lane doctrine need a representation in code, or is a declared bridge the correct expression of it?
Which automation engine owns which production trigger and write path? None is assigned.
risks: This repository is public. Bus state must carry mechanism and non-identifying status only; `npm run bus -- audit` enforces it, and a new rule is needed whenever a new identifier shape appears
Nothing polls. Freshness only improves when a sync is actually run, which is deliberate: an automatic poller would need stored credentials
A control plane that drifts from the systems it describes becomes confidently wrong; staleness reporting is the mitigation, not a cure
Lease overlap is exact-match by design; a resource named two different ways by two agents will not conflict when it should
dependencies: Node 22.6 or newer for native TypeScript execution
required_output: A verdict of PASS, PASS WITH CONDITIONS, FAIL or BLOCKED BY EVIDENCE on the kernel and the connector layer
Independent review of lane isolation, the approval boundary, lease conflict handling, event immutability, and whether the audit rules can be evaded by a realistic identifier shape
If PASS: implement task and handoff lifecycle helpers with tests, so tasks move between queued, active, blocked, review and completed under validation rather than by hand
A handoff packet written back to .neterverse/handoffs/codex-to-claude/
last_action: Connected the bus to all six systems of record with read-only calls, recorded each as a live observation, and confirmed 6/6 fresh with the committed-state audit clean.
next_action: Run npm test, then read src/lane.ts, src/risk.ts and src/audit.ts adversarially: try to find an input that crosses a lane, passes the approval boundary without a gate, or slips an external identifier past the audit into committed state.

rollback: The kernel and the bus are additive. Deleting packages/neterverse-kernel and .neterverse/ returns the repository to its prior state; no existing file's behaviour was changed.
